title: Argentina beyond Mendoza
subtitle: North and south
objectives: Name San Juan and other regions

steps.title: Salta
steps.body: In the far north, Salta's Calchaquí Valleys hold some of the world's highest vineyards, from 1,700 to over 3,000 m. Cafayate is the centre. Torrontés, a cross of Muscat of Alexandria and Criolla Chica, gives floral, aromatic whites. Malbec and Cabernet there are dark and intense, thanks to strong sun and cold nights.

steps.title: Patagonia
steps.body: In the south, Patagonia's Neuquén and Río Negro are low, about 300 m, but at 38 to 39 degrees south, cooled by latitude and strong winds. The wind keeps grapes healthy and thickens skins. Pinot Noir, Malbec and Merlot make fresher, more elegant wines than in Mendoza. Some Río Negro vines date from the early 20th century.

steps.prompt: What keeps Patagonia cool, compared with Salta?
steps.explanation: Patagonia is low, so its coolness comes from latitude and constant wind.

steps.body: The same grape, Malbec, from Salta, Mendoza and Patagonia makes a great tasting lesson. Altitude, latitude and wind each leave a mark.

steps.prompt: Which statements about Salta are true?
steps.explanation: Mendoza is by far Argentina's largest region.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Salta has vineyards up to 3,000 m and floral Torrontés
Patagonia is cooled by latitude and wind
Argentina's styles vary with altitude and latitude
